facts.text: Haugan was named after H.G., the railroad’s land commissioner and comptroller who secured the line’s rights‑of‑way.
Established around 1908, Haugan served as a critical pusher station, attaching extra steam locomotives to help trains climb the 2.2% grades of the Bitterroot Range.
The Savenac Nursery Historic District, founded in 1907, once produced up to 12 million seedlings annually for national forests before closing.
When the Milwaukee Road electrified its Pacific Extension in 1919, Haugan’s role as a steam helper station faded, leading to its gradual decline.
Haugan was one of several towns destroyed during the Great Fire of 1910, a blaze that reshaped Montana’s western forests.
Haugan sits amid the Lolo National Forest, where the Regis River winds through the community’s scenic valley.
